typography_visual_philosophy.statement: Typography behaves as a brand-world information engine: an authored display identity anchors live process imagery while restrained claims, module labels, bilingual support and microcopy assign semantic roles across the campaign system.

stable_typography_grammar.statement: An approved expressive display-lettering asset provides identity mass without becoming a generic oversized brush headline.
Display, claim, narrative, label and microcopy roles use sharp scale and density separation so one headline does not carry the whole system.
A compact proposition/claim layer bridges identity and process imagery while remaining visibly subordinate to the display identity and hero action.
Module labels identify process, ingredient, place or world roles; label geometry follows semantic zones rather than decoration-only placement.
Chinese remains the identity and narrative authority while compact Latin support contributes cadence without competing for first read.

variation_axes_typography.statement: Display-title content and approved glyph asset may change with brand identity while retaining high-mass irregular authored behavior.
Module count, label wording and support-copy density may adapt to available semantic roles; exact three-module geometry is not required.
Exact dark/hot/light color values may change while preserving contrast roles and functional readability.

features: exact font files and distress instance

typography_content_compatibility.statement: A full-family execution needs enough truthful semantic content to support at least display identity, process/product narrative and a world/context information tier.
When only one isolated product image and one short title are available, the typography package must fail closed rather than simulate brand-world depth with filler copy.

renderer_responsibility: exploratory display-lettering direction only when a specialized visual-synthesis route is authorized
figma_responsibility: exact live Chinese and Latin copy
module labels and restrained vector marks
placement of an approved display-lettering asset

transfer_risks: generic brush collapse if the display asset is replaced by an unreviewed calligraphy font
brand-world collapse if support tiers are removed or filled with meaningless copy
cheap bilingual texture if Latin is used as decorative filler
wrong characters or brand leakage if source copy is reused across brands
unresolved_uncertainties: No typography-only transfer validation has established which display-lettering behavior survives new content.
No specific production font family is approved for functional Chinese or Latin roles.
Whole-image approval does not establish component approval for any typography mechanism.
